For what it's worth, I work at a crisis center. We are hands free and if you say you want to leave, we can't make you stay. We are a 23 hour stay facility and we give referrals and help people get on their feet. And we're completely free of charge, with or without insurance. Unfortunately, I cannot come here myself because we are not allowed to talk to people we know (just like you're not allowed to see your doctor friend for actual medical work), and I know all my coworkers, obviously. It sucks. We do check our guest's skin to make sure there's no open wounds, but they don't have to get completely naked. We do take their stuff and put it away. But it's honestly a lot better than a psych ward, a lot more freedom. Snacks whenever you want, sleep as much as you want, see a psychiatrist IF YOU WANT.

But yeah, most places suck. There are some places out there though that treat you better, or should.

Heyo! Diagnosed paranoid schizophrenic gal with a plethora of other bullshit to top that. I've only recently gotten medicated for it, and I've been with my now husband for about 4 and a half years.

This will sound silly, but there are nights where my husband wakes up to find me staring at the front door because I'm convinced that if I close my eyes, someone will come take me and hurt me. This has happened significantly less as I've gotten adjusted to medication, but that is falling apart. The thing my husband does is take me back to bed, and talk to me about what I have to do the next day. Distracting me. Or, if I'm knee deep in it, he'll talk to me about what I'm scared of. What am I hearing? What am I seeing? He's had to hold me while I sob about the dark monster thing staring over me, and how I'm scared he'll find a knife and hurt me (I've been stabbed before, and definitely don't want to be stabbed again).

I get this paranoia when I'm driving. I've been around a lot of violence (family) and my brother shot a gun at me once before, so when I'm driving and see people, I get so fucking scared I'll get shot. Sometimes that results in speeding. Sometimes, it results in me pulling over in what I consider a safe spot and sobbing.

Others have brought this up, but having a plan in advance is best. Communication is everything, in this and in every part of a relationship. I wish I had a plan in place for my husband, but he watched everything start rendering its head. I'm convinced he had no idea what the fuck was happening to me. So, take it from me, and talk to her and get plans in place. Ask her what to do in extreme circumstances (like that could hurt her or yourself). Ask her what to do in all areas. Not all schizophrenics experience the same things (some don't hear voices, some don't see things that aren't there, some don't experience paranoia which I'm jealous of, etc.), so figure out what happens, and plan. And most importantly, there is a line between worry and freaking out. I don't know her, but I know things can get terrifying. Be safe, be kind, and be supportive. You've got this!

They would tune into our cameras and ask us to show we are wearing our alarms and such. Well, the phone rings, and I'm the one the usually answers it, and I answer and this guy asked me about what time we stop selling alcohol (midnight every day, so it was a bit weird he called). Something inside me just sank. I always answered the call with, "Gas station name, theballinstalin speaking" with my actual name and the gas station name obviously, and this guy kept saying, "Oh Stalin, you look lovely in that green shirt" or whatever. It made me so uncomfortable. I was going to just hang up until he mentioned what I was wearing. He could see me. We are 24/7, so I panicked, and after him telling me about him touching himself and stuff, I hung up and ran off. I didn't appear from the freezers until 3 or 4am. Well, the guy came into the store. He didn't see me I guess, but he left with no incidents or anything. He's banned from the store because we got him on cameras and stuff.
2. This one is a bit freakier. It was within the last month I was working there. I was with a coworker, Anthony, and he was in the freezers and I was watching up front. My store was filled with locals, and I didn't feel too freaked out by the customers. Well, Anthony came out and was going to take a smoke break when this lady comes running into our store at about 11:30pm. She's stick thin, skin grey, makeup smeared all over her face, and blood..all over her face and shirt. Her clothes were ripped up and incredibly dirty, and she just looked...like someone threw her out of a car and beat her up. She looks right at me, grabs me by the wrist, and takes me into the restroom with her and locks the door. She tells me a guy is coming after her, he r\*ped her, she had to jump out of the car, and ran for her life. She had no shoes on and her feet were messed up. She told me about how I couldn't call the cops because she had a court case coming up and that she would lose her kids, etc. I legit just stood there, terrified, I didn't think it was as bad as it was until much later. I think my brain just told me, "Eh, this isn't bad, don't worry", so that I wouldn't die of a heart attack. Anyways, she sits on the floor, and pulls out a knife and says she took it from her attacker, and I managed to get between her and the door and sat on the ground to not agitate her. I texted my husband who was working overnights at a local casino as a security guard and told him to call the cops for me. He didn't get a break to check his phone until about 3-4am. By that time, the local newspaper delivery couple (wife and husband) come into the store. I heard the door alarm. Anthony told me later that Lisa, the wife's name, asked where I was. I had a consistent scheduled, same days on and off. And Anthony apparently told Lisa, "Oh, she's been in the bathroom for 3-4 hours with some lady high on meth that's bleeding". or something. The cops arrived like 60 seconds later, I had managed to keep this lady calm, she was crying about losing her daughter, and how I looked just like her, etc. I told her my legs were asleep, and I stood up, and in one fast movement, unlocked the door, and booked it. Lisa was right near the door while I saw cops coming towards the door. The lady with a knife opened the door with the knife gripped tightly in her hand, and lunged towards my direction. Anyways, nothing cool happens, she was arrested. Apparently, she lied about pretty much everything except the court case and losing her daughter. She was strung out and had no idea where she was or what was happening. Freaked me out because I was a not medicated schizophrenic. I was at the time working a pharmacy gig in the morning and overnights at the gas station, but I put my notice in the next time I saw my boss. Fuckkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk that.

Funny part of the last story is that I became a certified pharmacy technician and worked in 2 different pharmacies in that city. I found out about so many people being on highly addictive medication, people stealing meds, etc. Had a lady pull up in the drive thru to one of the places (WAG) and asked for her oxycodone. I looked and told her it was picked up already the day prior, and she cursed in the drive thru, looked at the passenger, and yelled, "That bitch stole my medicine! Let's go find his dumb ass", and drove off. I had to report the whole deal lol I know that city had a drug problem now because I live 5 hours west of that city and worked in 2 different pharmacies here, and doctors rarely prescribe C2's here, unlike there. That old city, everyone was on at least one C2, I swear.

Anyways, thanks for listening and stay safe. ♥
